sections.title: The law in brief
notes: Congress writes its own rules, and it should police its own members' false public statements. The full argument is in The Great American Betrayal.

sections.title: 1. What gets in (Fake News Exposed)
notes: A claim about President Trump or his administration that is unfavorable to him or them.

Proven false: the claim was corrected, retracted or settled; a court, the DOJ, an inspector general or the FEC found it false; or a major fact-checker rated it False, Mostly False, Pants on Fire or Four Pinocchios.
Rated misleading: rated misleading, missing context or Three Pinocchios (or equivalent).

Re-verification (Sep 24, 2026): every case was re-checked against its original record. 129 were verified by Swamp Force; 131 are listed as "Still being checked" and are not counted; 2 moved to Unsupported; 1 was removed. A fact-checker is never our proof, only a second confirmation. How we picked our fact-checkers.
Unproven claims are left out. Claims that were reviewed and could not be supported are listed separately on Not Yet Verified.

sections.title: Fact-checkers
notes: A fact-checker is never our proof, only a second confirmation after we check the original record. The 7 tests and all 16 results: How we picked our fact-checkers.

sections.title: 4. Party ledgers and J6
notes: A party-ledger row appears only after both its claim and its record are confirmed. A row that duplicates a Fake News case links to that case instead of repeating it.

sections.title: 5. Scorecard
notes: Every figure comes from an official source (BLS, CBP, Treasury, CBO, USDA, SSA, CMS, a city comptroller) and is tagged with who held power at the time. Until a figure is confirmed against its source, it is marked Under review and shows no number.

sections.title: 6. Fact and opinion
notes: Opinion appears only on the Opinion page and in blocks labeled or "Our view." Everything else is sourced on the page.

sections.title: 7. Corrections
notes: Found an error? Email editor@swampforce.com with the case number and the source. Confirmed errors are fixed and noted.

sections.title: 8. How balanced is this site?
notes: Every rated item on the site, counted by the side of the person or outlet that made the claim. Raw counts only. A catalog case is assigned to the first entity named in its "Who pushed it" field; party follows official affiliation; strategists, PACs, advocacy groups and commentators without party office count as Independent / other. Scorecard figures are data points, not rated claims, and are not counted.

Catalog cases that name a Democrat anywhere in the pusher field: 81; a Republican: 4. The catalog covers only claims about President Trump or his administration that are unfavorable to him or them (section 1).

Media outlets by name: The New York Times 3, The Washington Post 3, ABC News 2, Associated Press 2, BuzzFeed News 2, CNN 2, CNBC 1, City Journal 1, Der Spiegel 1, McClatchy 1, NBC News 1, NPR 1, Politico 1, TIME 1, The Daily Beast 1, The Guardian 1, The Morning Call 1, The U.S. Sun 1.

lawmakers-5.title: The First Amendment protects much false speech
lines: United States v. Alvarez (2012) struck down the Stolen Valor Act, and the plurality wrote that "falsity alone may not suffice to bring the speech outside the First Amendment." A public official suing over a falsehood about official conduct must prove "actual malice," meaning knowledge of falsity or reckless disregard of the truth (New York Times Co. v. Sullivan, 1964). The Speech or Debate Clause (art. I, § 6) protects legislative acts. It did not cover a senator's private publication of the Pentagon Papers (Gravel v. United States, 1972) or a senator's newsletters and press release (Hutchinson v. Proxmire, 1979). Each House may discipline its own members (art. I, § 5).
